solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Illegally dispose of end of antenna?

definitions.meaning: to dump rubbish illegally by the roadside, a British verb
read playfully, the tip of an insect's feeler, the point of a housefly's antenna

explanation.surface: A cryptic question about getting rid of the end of an aerial unlawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: To fly-tip is British slang for dumping waste illegally; the second reading splits it into the tip of a fly, whose antenna has an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly-tipping is the British term for illegal dumping of rubbish on land not licensed for it.

clue.text: Ladies enjoy receiving two honours: double!

indicators.note: receiving means the pair of honours goes inside the two other words

parts.note: the ladies is a women's toilet, a loo
like means enjoy
king and ace are honour cards in bridge

explanation.surface: Women delighted to be given two awards at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a person who closely resembles another, a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Give up waiting for magazine

definitions.meaning: to stop after a set time with no response, as a computer connection does

explanation.surface: Someone loses patience waiting for a periodical to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Time Out is a well-known London listings magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A connection that stops waiting for a reply is said to time out, a computing idiom.

clue.text: Limit certificate assigned to film about drug

indicators.note: about means the rating goes round the drug letter

parts.note: PG is the parental guidance film rating
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Censors restrict a film's rating because it is about drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To peg prices is to fix or cap them, so to limit them.

clue.text: Surprise, abandoning a revoke

indicators.note: abandoning says the clue's single 'a' is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: to take aback is to surprise or startle

explanation.surface: A bridge player is startled to find a revoke has been made.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a revoke is failing to follow suit, which misdirects; here it is the verb meaning withdraw.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke a statement is to withdraw or retract it, a straight synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Material for printer part that one replaces

indicators.note: part signals that only a portion of the following words, run together, is taken

explanation.surface: Talking about printer supplies and the component a user swaps out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part that one replaces' looks like a cartridge description, but 'part' signals letters taken from inside 'that one replaces'.
explanation.definitionFit: The powdered ink used by laser printers and photocopiers is the substance they print with.

clue.text: In morning, asks for change: a lot of money

indicators.note: for change says the letters of these words are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone asks in the morning for small change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like coins, which fits 'money', but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge sum, as would be demanded to free a captured monarch, an idiom for a fortune.

clue.text: Very young capital abandoned by teacher for very old one

parts.note: a baby is very young

indicators.note: abandoned by means the teacher leaves the capital's name

parts.note: London is the UK capital
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A young city loses its academic in favour of an ancient one.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon is an ancient Mesopotamian capital city, so a very old capital.

clue.text: Absence of medical man upset genetic unit

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: no means none of, an absence
doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: The doctor's absence upsets everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet of nucleotides coding for one amino acid is a basic unit of DNA's code.

clue.text: Weapon of British soldier, good one

parts.note: Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is the traditional name for a British private
'un is a colloquial form of one, as in 'a good 'un'

explanation.surface: Praise for the gun carried by a fine British infantryman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thompson submachine gun is a firearm, so it is a weapon.

clue.text: Diarist's criticism of thin wine?

definitions.meaning: Charles Pooter, writer of The Diary of a ... by George and Weedon Grossmith; the 's is 'is'
a wine lacking fullness is said to have ...

explanation.surface: A diarist records a complaint about a watery wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody is a classic English comic novel whose diarist, Mr Pooter, is the nobody of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grossmiths' famous diarist is literally titled an unimportant person, the Nobody of the book.

clue.text: Opening this could be problem on farm: cows will wander

indicators.note: wandering cows stray out of place, so the letters of the farm words move about

explanation.surface: A warning that on a farm the cattle will roam if a gate is opened.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening a can of worms means starting off a tangle of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To open this tin of bait is the idiom for stirring up a mass of complications.

clue.text: Be unreasonably dissatisfied with bread and butter?

definitions.text: Be unreasonably dissatisfied with bread and butter?

parts.words: Be unreasonably dissatisfied with bread and butter?
parts.note: the idiom for being greedily discontent pictured literally as asking for a preserve on top of a buttered slice

explanation.surface: Someone is not content with plain buttered bread.
explanation.walkthrough: This British idiom describes demanding more than is reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to expect extras when the basics already offered should suffice.

clue.text: Join prison to be executed

indicators.note: executed by beheading, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the clink is slang for jail

explanation.surface: A convict is sent to prison to await execution.
explanation.definitionFit: To connect or couple two things is to join them, a plain synonym.

clue.text: One put in large order

indicators.note: put in means the numeral is placed within the other word

parts.note: fat means large in girth
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is placed in charge of a big order.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree, a command issued by authority.

clue.text: Head drops Irish briefly for very simple subjects?

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
rain is drops of water falling

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: A boss leaves Irish out of the timetable to make the subjects easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Decisions or questions needing no thought at all are what plain easy matters are called.

clue.text: Begging, get no end of a jolt

indicators.note: no end of means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a bump is a jolt

explanation.surface: Pleading and getting endless knocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge something, such as a cigarette, by asking is slang for acquiring it by begging.

clue.text: Solitary park hard to find without lead

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a park

indicators.note: without lead means the first letter is lost

parts.note: elusive means hard to find

explanation.surface: A lone dog in the park is hard to find without its lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit-like person who shuns company lives a lonely, withdrawn life.

clue.text: One or two authors: O and MR?

definitions.text: One or two authors: O and MR?

parts.words: One or two authors: O and MR?
parts.note: the writers O. Henry and M. R. James share the two names of the American-born novelist, once their initials are supplied

explanation.surface: A puzzle about writers known only by their initials.
explanation.walkthrough: O. Henry (short stories) and M. R. James (ghost stories) each give one name of the single novelist who wrote The Turn of the Screw.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist is one author whose name also comes from two other authors' surnames.

clue.text: I'm into great dancing, to this?

definitions.text: I'm into great dancing, to this?

indicators.note: into means the contraction goes inside the jumbled letters
dancing means the letters of 'great' move about

explanation.surface: A dancer says they love dancing to this music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' makes RAGTE from 'great', and 'into' puts IM inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The syncopated piano music of Scott Joplin's era was popular for dancing.

clue.text: Ride roughly cut

definitions.meaning: to go riding on horseback at an ordinary pace
to chop crudely, as with a blade

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut something on a rough ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses belong to one word: hacking out on a horse, and hacking at wood with an axe.

clue.text: On top of pier, ate fish

indicators.note: on top of in a down clue means the first word sits above the second

parts.note: had means ate
a dock is a pier or wharf

explanation.surface: Someone on a pier ate fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Atlantic food fish of the cod family, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Somehow obtain pounds to put in purse

indicators.note: to put in places the money symbol inside the other word

parts.note: a handbag, which Americans call a purse
L stands for pounds, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Somehow getting money together to put in a purse.
explanation.definitionFit: To blag is British slang for getting something by trickery or persuasion.

clue.text: Large investment has eroded capital? Lord!

indicators.note: has eroded capital means the head letter is worn away

parts.note: investment is an old military term for a siege

explanation.surface: A large investment has lost money, prompting an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks financial, but it means the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal superior owed allegiance is a lord.

clue.text: Neither too fat nor too thin for TV, say?

definitions.text: Neither too fat nor too thin
definitions.meaning: read as a medium mass, an average weight
television is an example of a means of broad public communication

explanation.surface: A query about a body shape that is neither heavy nor slight for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Television is one of the channels that reach a huge audience, an example of that kind of outlet.

clue.text: One interrupting top performer and music producer

indicators.note: interrupting means the numeral breaks into the other word

parts.note: a star is a top performer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone interrupts a famous performer and a record producer.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-necked Indian lute produces music, an instrument as a maker of sound.

clue.text: As it were, "unendorse" plan?

definitions.meaning: to take away a signature, a made-up word for undoing a sign-off

explanation.surface: A coined verb is offered for a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as DE-SIGN, the word looks like the undoing of signing, which is what unendorsing would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a drawing or scheme set out in advance, a synonym of a plan.

clue.text: Powerful sort of shift that may enthuse the CID?

parts.note: a tec is a detective, a member of the Criminal Investigation Department
a tonic is something that invigorates or lifts the spirits

explanation.surface: A boost that might energise detectives on a heavy work shift.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is Britain's plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Movements of the Earth's crustal plates are enormous, hence the phrase for a fundamental change.

clue.text: Sort of cake competition

definitions.meaning: a small cake baked in a paper case
a tournament with a trophy, like the FA's knockout

explanation.surface: A cake-baking contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout tournament is named after its trophy, and a small sponge cake shares the name.

clue.text: Succeeded the ruler of Hanover, say? It's his choice

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
Hanover's ruler held the title Elector of the Holy Roman Empire

explanation.surface: A line of succession to the throne of Hanover and who gets to pick.
explanation.walkthrough: Before becoming kings, Hanover's rulers were Electors who chose the Holy Roman Emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: A selector picks a team, so the choice of players is his to make.

clue.text: I may enter game with less room to manoeuvre

indicators.note: may enter has the single letter go inside the card game's name

parts.note: poker is a card game

explanation.surface: A player says they might join a game where space is tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Poky means small and cramped, so a more cramped room has less space.
